:::{#def-bit}
#### Bit (shannon)

A **bit**, also called a **shannon** (symbol Sh) [@iec80000132008], is the unit of information
when the logarithm in [surprisal](#def-surprisal),
and in every quantity built from it, has base $2$.

One bit is the surprisal of a [value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization) with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/2$:
for a value $x$ of a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
s(x) = 1 \text{ bit}
&\iff -\log_2 \P(X=x) = 1\\
&\iff \P(X=x) = 2^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

In words, a bit is the surprisal of the outcome of one binary trial
whose two outcomes are equally likely,
such as one toss of a fair coin.

:::
